hero.alt: A dark house with illuminated windows, each suggesting a different possible life, while several windows begin to go dark.

glossary.name: Beatitude
glossary.definition: Complete and final human fulfillment in God.

glossary.name: Beatific vision
glossary.definition: The immediate knowledge of God granted to the blessed; not exhaustive comprehension of the infinite by a finite mind.

glossary.name: Finite good
glossary.definition: A genuine but limited good capable of fulfilling a proportionate desire without becoming the whole meaning of existence.

glossary.name: Ultimate end
glossary.definition: The final good for whose sake other goods are desired and in which desire comes to rest.

glossary.name: Hedonic adaptation
glossary.definition: The tendency for emotional responses to changed circumstances to diminish or normalize over time, though not uniformly or completely.

glossary.name: Argument from desire
glossary.definition: The proposal that the structure of certain human longings may point beyond finite objects; in this essay, a clue rather than a stand-alone proof.

glossary.name: Idolatry
glossary.definition: Requiring a created good to perform the work of the ultimate good: to justify existence, secure identity completely, or defeat loss by its own power.

glossary.name: Ordered love
glossary.definition: Loving each created good according to its real worth and in relation to the source of its goodness.

glossary.name: Participation
glossary.definition: The classical claim that created things possess goodness finitely by sharing in a fullness they do not originate.

glossary.name: Naturalism
glossary.definition: The view that nature is the whole of reality and requires no transcendent source.

glossary.name: Redemption
glossary.definition: God's healing and transformation of what has been wounded, rather than the denial that the wound occurred.

glossary.name: St. Augustine
glossary.definition: North African bishop and author of the Confessions, whose account of the restless heart anchors the essay.

glossary.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
glossary.definition: Dominican theologian who distinguished imperfect earthly happiness from perfect beatitude in the vision of God.

glossary.name: Blaise Pascal
glossary.definition: Mathematician and Christian philosopher who wrote about diversion, misery, and the human attempt to fill itself with finite goods.

glossary.name: C. S. Lewis
glossary.definition: Christian essayist and literary critic whose treatments of Joy, desire, love, heaven, and grief provide the essay's chief literary influence.

glossary.name: Ludwig Feuerbach
glossary.definition: Nineteenth-century critic of religion who interpreted theology as the projection of idealized human qualities.

glossary.name: Sigmund Freud
glossary.definition: Founder of psychoanalysis, whose wish-fulfillment account treats religion as the continuation of the child's longing for protection.

glossary.name: Bernard Williams
glossary.definition: Secular moral philosopher whose Makropulos argument says endless life threatens boredom or the loss of personal identity.

visuals.title: The roads we do not take
visuals.label: UNLIVED FUTURES
visuals.caption: Every chosen life stands beside the translucent roads it closed.
visuals.alt: A single road passes many translucent side roads that fade into a blue-black horizon.

visuals.title: Three meanings of enough
visuals.label: THE WORD IN QUESTION
visuals.caption: A good can answer its proper desire without becoming the final answer to existence.

visuals.title: Even a full cup has an edge
visuals.label: FINITE GOOD
visuals.caption: The limit of a good does not make the good false.
visuals.alt: A full glass of water whose rim becomes the horizon of a tiny luminous landscape.

visuals.title: The candle and the sun
visuals.label: CREATION
visuals.caption: A candle can warm the room without being asked to become the sun.
visuals.alt: A candle warms a dark room while the first suggestion of sunrise appears beyond a window.

visuals.title: The cottage and the cathedral
visuals.label: IDOLATRY
visuals.caption: A finite good can be beautiful and still be crushed by the work it was never built to do.

visuals.title: Too much weight for one house
visuals.label: FINITE WEIGHT
visuals.caption: The cottage is not a failure because it cannot carry a cathedral.
visuals.alt: A small warm cottage buckles beneath the impossible architectural weight of a vast cathedral.

visuals.title: Sour grapes in stained glass
visuals.label: THE COPE OBJECTION
visuals.caption: The accusation is beautiful enough to deserve a real answer.
visuals.alt: A fox reaches toward grapes in a restrained stained-glass panel set in a dark stone frame.

visuals.title: The real and the simulated
visuals.label: WHAT REMAINS
visuals.caption: Explaining the origin of a desire does not settle whether the desire's object is real.
visuals.alt: A person faces an artificial beloved in a glass reflection while an imperfect real figure stands outside it.

visuals.title: What the explanation leaves standing
visuals.label: THE REMAINING QUESTION
visuals.caption: Mechanism, meaning, and truth are related questions, but they are not interchangeable.

visuals.title: A needle toward the unseen north
visuals.label: THE RESTLESS HEART
visuals.caption: A clue is not a demonstration, but neither is it nothing.
visuals.alt: An old brass compass with a heart-shaped needle turning toward an unseen north.

visuals.title: From desire to question
visuals.label: A CLUE, NOT A PROOF
visuals.caption: The argument from desire becomes strongest when it admits what it cannot establish on its own.

visuals.title: The wound is not erased
visuals.label: REDEMPTION
visuals.caption: The final hope is healing and transformation, not the claim that nothing was ever lost.
visuals.alt: A luminous wounded hand holds a cracked golden cup whose fractures let warm light into a dark room.

visuals.title: Possession and gift
visuals.label: ORDERED LOVE
visuals.caption: The same good can be clutched as a possession or received as a gift.

visuals.title: Grief and light in the same room
visuals.label: THE UNLIVED LIFE
visuals.caption: Light does not sentimentalize grief; it makes the room visible without taking the loss away.
visuals.alt: A quiet hospital room with a plastic water jug, an occupied chair, and dawn light entering through a window.

visuals.title: The hand that has let go
visuals.label: THE WORLD IS NOT ENOUGH
visuals.caption: The first credible light before sunrise: not escape from creation, but a world renewed.
visuals.alt: An adult hand remains at bicycle-seat height while a child rides toward a restrained dawn.

pulls.quote: Nobody gets every life. This is not a punishment handed out to people who failed. It is the flat arithmetic of being one person, in one body, moving one direction through time.
pulls.label: THE FLAT ARITHMETIC OF BEING ONE PERSON

pulls.quote: Maybe heaven is just the name we give to the lives we cannot bear not to have lived.
pulls.label: THE OBJECTION

pulls.quote: Even a full cup has an edge.
pulls.label: A FINITE GOOD

pulls.quote: The world's pleasures are not lies. The world's truths are mortal. That is the problem.
pulls.label: THE CENTRAL DISTINCTION

pulls.quote: An idol is normally a good thing that has been handed a job it was never built to do.
pulls.label: THE WEIGHT OF IDOLATRY

pulls.quote: Add incense and stained glass and sixteen hundred years of very good philosophy and sour grapes starts to look a great deal like sanctity.
pulls.label: THE ACCUSATION AT FULL STRENGTH

pulls.quote: Desire is a clue. It is not a demonstration.
pulls.label: THE EPISTEMIC LIMIT

pulls.quote: Lament is the sound hope makes when the promised good is not here yet.
pulls.label: THE RESTLESS HEART

pulls.quote: Redemption is necessary precisely because some things are not good.
pulls.label: THE WOUND REMAINS REAL

pulls.quote: Created things are not too small to love. They are too small to be God.
pulls.label: THE FINAL DISTINCTION
